12.passage: Exponential Probability Distribution in Service Queues

questions.question: Waiting time X in minutes at a tech support desk follows an exponential distribution with rate parameter λ = 0.2 (mean waiting time = 5 minutes). The cumulative distribution function is P(X ≤ x) = 1 - e⁻⁰ˑ²ˣ. What is the probability that a customer waits MORE than 10 minutes?

12.passage: Standard Normal Distribution (Z-Scores)

questions.question: Graduate Record Exam (GRE) scores are normally distributed with mean μ = 150 and standard deviation σ = 10. A candidate scores 170. What is the candidate's Z-score and what percentage of test-takers score below this candidate?

12.passage: Central Limit Theorem in Quality Sampling

questions.question: Lightbulb lifespans have a mean μ = 1000 hours and standard deviation σ = 100 hours. A random sample of n = 100 bulbs is drawn. By the Central Limit Theorem, what is the standard error (σ_x̅) of the sample mean?

12.passage: Confidence Interval Construction for Population Mean

questions.question: A sample of 100 batteries yields a sample mean life x̅ = 50 hours with sample standard error 0.5 hours. For a 95% confidence level (Z* = 1.96), what is the margin of error and resulting confidence interval for population mean μ?

12.passage: Hypothesis Testing P-Value Concept

questions.question: A pharmaceutical company tests a new drug claiming to reduce blood pressure. The null hypothesis H₀ states the drug has no effect. The statistical test yields a p-value of 0.02. At a standard significance level α = 0.05, what conclusion should be drawn?

options.text: Fail to reject H₀; drug is ineffective.
Reject H₀; there is statistically significant evidence the drug is effective.
Accept H₀; drug has a 98% failure rate.

12.passage: Poison Probability Distribution for Network Traffic

questions.question: Data packets arrive at a server at an average rate of λ = 3 packets per millisecond following a Poisson distribution P(X = k) = (e⁻λ λᵏ) / k!. What is the probability that exactly 2 packets arrive in a given millisecond? (Use e⁻³ ≈ 0.0498)

12.passage: Type I and Type II Errors in Medical Screening

questions.question: In medical hypothesis testing, the null hypothesis H₀ is "The patient is healthy." What constitutes a Type I Error in this decision-making framework?

options.text: Diagnosing a healthy patient as sick (False Positive)
Diagnosing a sick patient as healthy (False Negative)
